question: The earliest audiometric sign of noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) is a notch at 4000 Hz on the pure tone audiogram, with relative recovery at 8000 Hz, reflecting preferential damage to the basal cochlear hair cells that encode high-frequency sounds.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. NIHL signature = 4 kHz notch on PTA with recovery at 8 kHz. This is an SNHL pattern caused by cochlear outer hair cell damage at the basal turn. The 4 kHz notch is both a diagnostic marker and a screening tool for early occupational NIHL — important for NPPCD implementation in industrial settings.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The 4 kHz notch is pathognomonic of NIHL. The basal cochlear hair cells (encoding 3000-6000 Hz) are most vulnerable to acoustic trauma because they are exposed to maximum basilar membrane displacement from the amplified resonance of the ear canal. The notch at 4 kHz with partial recovery at 8 kHz is the earliest and most reliable marker for occupational noise exposure and is the basis for pre-employment audiometry in high-noise industries.
